aiOverview.content: The University of Hawaiʻi (UH) is a public, co-educational higher education system comprising 10 campuses across six islands in the state of Hawaiʻi. Established as a single campus in 1907, the system now includes three four-year universities and seven community colleges, serving approximately 49,977 students. Its flagship institution, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, is a leading "R1" research university and one of only three institutions in the U.S. to hold land-, sea-, space-, and sun-grant designations. University System Overview The UH System offers over 200 degree programs, ranging from short-term certificates and associate degrees to doctoral and professional degrees in law and medicine. Popular Majors at UH Mānoa: Psychology, Marketing, Nursing, Finance, and Biology. Distinctive Fields: Astronomy, East Asian Languages, Comparative Philosophy, and Ocean and Earth Sciences. Professional Schools: Includes the Shidler College of Business, School of Architecture, and schools of Law and Medicine. Online Education: UH Online offers over 40 degree and certificate programs across the system. Admissions Highlights Admissions criteria vary by campus and specific college within the system. UH Mānoa: Moderately selective with an acceptance rate around 70–87%. Admitted students typically have a mid-range GPA of 3.49–4.04. While SAT (1130–1350) and ACT (21–29) scores are considered, the university follows a test-optional policy. UH West Oʻahu: Generally requires a 2.7 cumulative high school GPA for automatic admission for freshmen. Transfer Students: Generally require at least 24 transferable credits with a minimum GPA (2.5 for Mānoa, 2.0 for West Oʻahu).
